newsitem.title: UK: UK to host Europe's biggest literary festival.
newsitem.headline: UK to host Europe's biggest literary festival.

text.p: Britain announced plans on Monday for Europe's biggest ever literature festival, uniting writers from around the world in a 10-day celebration of words.

"London is the world's cultural capital and a literary festival on this scale is long overdue. The festival will attract everyone, from the youngest reader to the confirmed bibliophile -- and not just from London but from around the globe," festival chairman Bing Taylor said in a statement.
The festival will be held in May 1999 and will include performances, readings, talks and experimental workshops.

Writer Doris Lessing, a member of the festival council, said London was just the place for this "feast of books and the arts" and predicted that readers and writers would come from around the world to celebrate both the literature and the city itself.

Events would take place at landmark buildings in literary London, while clubs, theatres, parks, museums and bookshops would be used in a diverse festival spanning music, cabaret, concerts and exhibitions.

"The London Festival of Literature will celebrate written and oral literature in all its forms, with the widest possible international audience...reflecting London's cosmopolitan nature and its unrivalled cultural strengths," said the organisers.
